summary: This diff does not touch .github/workflows/** and is a pure YAML edit (ai-os/MASTER_INDEX.yaml only), so no workflow-scope concerns apply, and the file parses as valid YAML with no duplicate ids. However, the change is far larger and riskier than the commit message claims ('close 7 real coverage gaps' -- actually adds 54 new registries entries, going from 50 to 104) and it introduces two concrete regressions in the one file whose entire job is being the authoritative 'check here before you duplicate work' index. First, three previously-registered LIVE entries -- snip_token_reduction_hook, prompt_registry_version_lifecycle_extension, and litert_spike_browser_execution_prior_art -- were silently deleted with zero mention in the commit message and zero trace anywhere in the new file (verified via full-text grep for their underlying artifacts: .snip/filters, prompt-os-service.ts/promptVersions, and litert-spike -- all zero hits). A future session reading this file has no way to discover these real, live mechanisms exist, defeating the file's own stated protocol ('query this file for an existing match... do not create a parallel mechanism') and risking exactly the duplicate-work failure mode this file exists to prevent. Second, the file's own header mandates regenerating quick_reference after any registries: edit ('quick_reference is REGENERATED, not hand-maintained... rerun generate_quick_reference.py after any registries: edit'), but quick_reference was left completely stale: it still has only 42 entries and gained zero new ids, meaning none of the 54 newly-added registries entries -- including the 7 the commit specifically highlights (veri_chat, browser_intent_cache, umr_tasks_registry, sap_reports_projexa_completion_effort, cron_systemd_consolidation_2026_07_29, utm_traceability_convention, capability_services_pair) plus major architecture entries (engines_gateways_architecture, self_sustaining_system_engine, owner_ai_protocol, metadata_engine_reconciliation, auditor_engine, wiring_engine) -- are reachable via the documented 'scan quick_reference first' workflow. quick_reference also lost 8 ids outright (including the 3 deleted entries plus ai_engineering_policy, audit198_framework, credit_spend_governance, rules_articles_198, standing_task_directive, which still exist in registries but are now unreachable via quick_reference). Net effect: the task claims to close coverage gaps but instead leaves the central index in a worse discoverability state than before for roughly 60% of its own entries, and permanently loses 3 real ones.
issues: Silently deleted 3 live registry entries (snip_token_reduction_hook, prompt_registry_version_lifecycle_extension, litert_spike_browser_execution_prior_art) with no explanation and no trace left anywhere in the file -- restore them or explicitly justify removal.

quick_reference was not regenerated despite 54 new registries entries being added (registries grew 50->104, quick_reference gained 0 new ids and lost 8, including the 3 deleted ones) -- violates this file's own documented self-maintenance protocol and makes most of the new content undiscoverable via the intended workflow.

Commit message materially understates the change's scope ('close 7 real coverage gaps' vs. the actual 54 new registries entries added), which likely let the quick_reference regression and the 3 silent deletions go unnoticed by the task's own self-review.
Does not touch .github/workflows/** -- no workflow-scope push concern applies to this diff.
